battle.name: 唐滅高昌
battle.brief: 貞觀十四年（640）八月，唐以兵部尚書侯君集為交河道行軍大總管，率兵及回紇、西域諸國十餘萬眾西征高昌。大軍進圍交河城時，高昌王麴文泰已卒，其子麴智盛出降，唐得其城二十二座、戶八千四十六。卡面的羅馬扭力投石機早此役八百九十年，攻城所倚的是唐軍的雲梯、撞車與拋車，即中國式的投石機。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場戰爭是唐太宗貞觀十四年（640）對西域高昌國的滅國之戰，交戰雙方是唐與麴氏高昌。唐方由兵部尚書侯君集任交河道行軍大總管，節制漢兵、回紇兵與西域諸國提供的蕃兵，帳下有薛萬均、牛進達、契苾何力等將領，兵部與御史臺派員隨軍監察，糧餉由河西的涼州、瓜州、敦煌一路節度供應，出玉門關之後改用駱駝與牛車轉運；兵種以步騎為主，另設專門的攻城器械隊隨大軍同行。高昌一方是漢人麴氏建立的城邦王國，都交河城，另有柳中、蒲昌、田地、天泉等城，境內灌溉渠網與屯田密集，賦役兵制脫胎漢晉舊制，居民以漢魏晉屯戍軍民後裔為主，夾雜昭武九姓的粟特僑民。麴文泰在位時與西突厥結盟，倚仗外勢拒絕唐使通商；唐軍四周還有焉耆、龜茲等鄰國環繞，而回紇與西域諸國此次站在唐軍一方作戰，中原與西域的力量第一次在同一條戰線上直接碰撞。
countriesEn: This war was the destruction of the western state of Gaochang by the Tang court in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan (640) under Emperor Taizong, and the two sides were the Tang and the Qu-ruled kingdom of Gaochang. On the Tang side the command was given to the Minister of War Hou Junji as General of the March for the Jiaohe Route; he held command over Han troops, Huige (Uighur) soldiers and auxiliaries furnished by the states of the western regions, and his roster included such generals as Xue Wanjun, Niu Jinda and Qibi Heli, with officials of the Ministry of War and the Censorate attached to the army to supervise it. Supplies came up through Liangzhou, Guazhou and Dunhuang along the Hexi corridor, and beyond the Yumen Pass the baggage was shifted to camels and ox carts. The force was infantry and cavalry, with a separate corps of siege equipment moving with the main body. Gaochang on the other side was a city-state kingdom founded by Han Chinese and ruled by the Qu family, with its capital at Jiuhe and other towns at Liuzhong, Puchang, Tiandi and Tianquan; a dense network of irrigation channels and state farms covered its territory, its fiscal and military institutions were modelled on those of the Han and Jin, and its people were chiefly the descendants of garrison soldiers and settlers of Han, Wei and Jin times, mixed with Sogdian colonists of the Zhaoju Nine Surnames. While Qu Wentai held the throne he had allied with the Western Turks and leaned on that external support to refuse Tang envoys and to obstruct Tang trade. Around the theatre sat other states such as Yanqi and Kucha, while the Huige and the remaining states of the western regions fought on the Tang side; the central plains and the western regions collided for the first time on a single front.
people: 下詔出兵的是唐太宗李世民。貞觀十三年冬，朝廷決定用武力解決高昌問題，太宗把交河道行軍大總管的印綬交給侯君集，這位以勇武知名、出身行伍的兵部尚書此前並無大軍團攻城的經驗，卻是最能服眾的宿將。攻城細節也由他定：大軍進抵柳中，他不願再等，連夜架雲梯登城；高昌王麴文泰在兵臨城下的憂懼中發病而死，其子麴智盛嗣位，一度遣使議降而不得應允，最後城破出降。麴文泰在位時與西突厥結盟、阻絕西域朝貢使者，又厚待西行求法的玄奘，其陵墓營造之豪奢在唐廷眼中是失臣之禮，詔令停用其過分營造。麴智盛降後授官封爵、留居京師。事後侯君集因軍中私取官物、未能禁制將士競盜而遭人揭發下獄，褚遂良上封事論其貪污，太宗乃貶其官，使他與李靖那樣的功臣相比而不得拜相，怨望由此種下禍根。
peopleEn: The order to send the army was Emperor Taizong's, Li Shimin's. In the winter of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan the court decided to settle the question of Gaochang by force, and the emperor handed the tally of General of the March for the Jiaohe Route to Hou Junji, a Minister of War of fighting stock who had no experience of taking a walled city with a great army but was the most trusted of the seasoned commanders. The details of the assault were also his: when the army reached Liuzhong he was unwilling to wait longer and had the scaling ladders planted by night; Qu Wentai, the king of Gaochang, died of the illness that fear and the approach of the army had brought on, and his son Qu Zhisheng succeeded him, at one point sent an envoy to treat for surrender and was refused, and finally came out of the city and surrendered when it was breached. While Qu Wentai reigned he had allied with the Western Turks, had obstructed the envoys of the western states, and had treated the pilgrim Xuanzang lavishly on his westward journey; the extravagant building of his tomb was regarded at court as the presumption of a subject, and an edict ordered the excessive works stopped. After his surrender Qu Zhisheng was granted office and rank and was kept at the capital. Afterwards Hou Junji was accused of taking the property of the conquered state and of failing to stop his soldiers from plundering, was impeached and imprisoned, and Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial charging him with covetousness; the emperor therefore demoted him, so that measured against a man of Li Jing's achievements he was passed over for the highest ministry, and from that slight the seed of his misfortune was sown.
kits: 卡面這件投石機是羅馬帝國的扭力式石砲，學名 onager 或 scipio：一支長臂安在木架上，臂端繫兜，靠絞緊的韌索儲蓄扭力，發射時把石彈甩出，射程可達數百步，用來砸城牆、壓制城頭守軍並把石塊拋入城內。它的紀年是公元前250年，比這場戰爭早了近九百年，而且是地中海世界的器械，不會出現在交河城下。現場真正服役的是唐軍自造的一套攻城器械：拋車是當時中國式的投石機，以人力牽引擺臂拋石，負責打擊城牆與城頭；撞車是覆以皮革與木板的巨車，專撞城門與牆根；雲梯供士卒登城；弩機與床弩在城下排成弩陣，覆蓋城頭火位；巢車是隨軍可望的高台，居高觀察敵情。步兵用刀與槊，騎兵用馬，攻城大軍另備牛車與橐駝運糧，高昌方面的守軍以弓弩為主，也備石砲反擊，城牆是夯土築成、四周有灌溉水渠與壕溝可資遮蔽，城內存粟麥、葡萄、凍酒、刺蜜、白面與疊布，足以支撐一場短期的圍城。
kitsEn: The engine on the card is the Roman torsion stone-thrower, known as the onager or the scipio: a long throwing arm mounted on a timber frame, with a sling at its tip, storing torsional energy in tightly twisted skeins of sinew and flinging a stone bolt out on a trajectory reaching several hundred paces, used to smash walls, sweep the parapet of defenders and lob stones into the town. Its date is 250 BC, nearly nine centuries earlier than this war, and it is a Mediterranean machine that could not have stood beneath the walls of Jiuhe. What actually went into service was the set of siege engines built by the Tang army itself: the paoche was the Chinese stone-thrower of the time, worked by human traction on a throwing beam, and its business was to batter the walls and the parapet; the chongche was a great cart sheathed in hide and timber for ramming gates and the foot of the wall; the scaling ladders let the men climb the face; crossbow engines and heavy crossbows were ranged in a battery below the walls to sweep the parapet; and the watch-towers were tall platforms carried with the army for observing the enemy. Infantry carried sabres and spears, cavalry rode horses, and the besieging host kept ox carts and camels for the grain. The garrison of Gaochang fought mainly with bow and crossbow and also had stone-throwers of its own for answering fire; its walls were rammed earth ringed by irrigation channels and ditches that served as cover, and inside the town stood wheat and millet, grapes, frozen wine, honey combed from the flowers, white flour and cotton cloth, enough to sustain a siege of short duration.
tactics: 唐軍的部署是典型的西域遠征形制：主力自長安出發，沿河西走廊經涼州、瓜州至敦煌，出玉門關後分前隊、中軍、後隊，糧車居中，井渠隨軍開鑿，抵柳中時已深入戈壁數千餘里。攻城採兩段式：白日以弩陣封鎖城頭、以拋車擊打城牆與城頭守軍、以撞車撞擊城門，夜晚趁城頭火光與聲息混雜之際架雲梯登城，牛進達一系先登上城頭，隨即破門而入，麴智盛出降。城破之後，大軍分道略地，收其城二十二座，錄取戶口，置官鎮守，安排屯田，然後班師。高昌的抵抗則以拖延與死守為主：唐軍進逼時曾在柳中一線出兵迎拒，退入交河城後依託夯土城牆、灌溉水渠與井泉固守，城頭布弓弩手與石砲，並屢遣使議降以圖緩兵；同時倚仗西突厥的外援作為虛張之勢。外交線上，唐廷一面詔令西域諸國出兵助唐以孤立高昌，一面遣使分說，企圖在兵臨城下之際不戰而屈人之兵，卻最終選擇了破城。
tacticsEn: The Tang deployment followed the standard pattern of a far-western expedition. The main body left Chang'an, ran along the Hexi corridor through Liangzhou and Guazhou to Dunhuang, and once past the Yumen Pass was divided into vanguard, centre and rearguard, with the grain wagons in the middle and wells dug as the column moved; by the time it reached Liuzhong it had already pushed several thousand li into the gravel desert. The siege was worked in two stages: by day a battery of crossbows locked down the parapet, the paoche battered the walls and the defenders on top of them, and the chongche rammed the gate; by night, in the confusion of torchlight and noise on the rampart, the scaling ladders were planted and the men of Niu Jinda's column got over first, the gate was forced, and Qu Zhisheng came out and surrendered. After the city fell the army was split to take the countryside, gathered in twenty-two towns, recorded the households, set up officials to hold them, arranged farms, and then marched home. Gaochang's resistance took the form of delay and a stubborn defence: it put troops into the field to meet the advancing army around Liuzhong, then withdrew into the city of Jiuhe and held fast behind rammed-earth walls, irrigation channels and wells, with bowmen and stone-throwers posted on the parapet, and it sent envoys to treat for surrender again and again in the hope of buying time, while leaning on the West Turks as a support to be seen but not necessarily to be there. On the diplomatic side the court enjoined the states of the western regions to send troops against Gaochang so as to isolate it, and sent envoys to argue the case in the hope of bending the enemy without a blow; in the end it chose the breach.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。征高昌之師，兵部尚書侯君集所部連同回紇與西域諸國之兵，總計十餘萬眾（《資治通鑑》《新唐書》均作十餘萬眾之語），其中核心的漢軍人數遠少於此，回紇與諸蕃多擔任騎兵、護糧與向導之役。高昌方面，《新唐書·西域傳》記其有兵三萬餘人，馬匹數萬，境內二十二城，穀麥再熟，以鹽、絲織品、凍酒知名；城破之後唐廷錄得的數目是城二十二座、戶八千四十六、口一萬七千七百。行程方面，大軍自長安出發，經涼州、瓜州、敦煌，出玉門關後至交河約三千餘里，全程多在瀚海與戈壁之中，汲水與運糧是最大的消耗。時間線是：貞觀十三年冬奉命出兵與集兵，貞觀十四年正月大軍西行，八月進圍交河城並破之，其後置西州、置安西都護府於交河、詔葬麴文泰於長安北原，並封麴智盛官爵。戰損方面，唐軍與高昌軍的陣亡數字均不見確載；可以確定的是遠征深入、糧運艱難，軍中紀律也曾失控，侯君集班師之後即因私取官物被人告發。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The army that campaigned against Gaochang, with the troops of the Huige and of the western states counted in, numbered more than a hundred thousand men, in the words used alike by the Zizhi Tongjian and the Xinshu; the Han core of that host was far smaller, the Huige and the other auxiliaries serving mostly as cavalry, as escort for the grain and as guides. On the Gaochang side the Xinshu liezhuan of the western regions records more than thirty thousand men under arms, several tens of thousands of horses, twenty-two towns in the territory, wheat and millet that ripened twice a year, and a land famous for its salt, its silk stuffs and its frozen wine. After the city fell, the Tang court drew up the tally at twenty-two towns, eight thousand and forty-six households and seventeen thousand seven hundred persons. As for distance, the army left Chang'an, passed through Liangzhou, Guazhou and Dunhuang, and from beyond the Yumen Pass still had some three thousand li to go before reaching Jiuhe, the greater part of the way across desert and gravel; drawing water and carrying grain were the largest drains on the force. The chronology runs: the order to campaign and the mustering of the army in the winter of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, the westward march in the first month of the fourteenth, the investment of Jiuhe and its capture in the eighth month, and thereafter the establishment of Xizhou, the setting up of the Protectorate of the Western Regions at Jiuhe, the edict for the burial of Qu Wentai on the northern plain of Chang'an, and the grant of office and rank to Qu Zhisheng. On losses there is no reliable figure, for the Tang army or for the forces of Gaochang; what is certain is that the expedition went deep and that carrying grain was hard, that discipline in the host at times broke down, and that Hou Junji was impeached for taking the property of the conquered state as soon as he returned.
cause: 導火線是麴文泰阻斷了西域的朝貢通道。貞觀年間唐的使團與商旅要從敦煌往西，經高昌、焉耆、龜茲通往西域諸國，高昌正卡在天山南北孔道的咽喉；麴文泰既與西突厥結盟，又不接受唐廷的約束，使者前往屢遭冷遇，這在以天可汗自居的唐看來，是對朝覲秩序的挑釁。此前西行求法的玄奘曾受麴文泰厚待，也正說明這個城邦的存亡繫於絲路的位置與唐廷的態度。深一層看，高昌是漢人移民建立的城邦，國勢來自灌溉農業與商道樞紐，麴氏一族害怕內附會失去國格，因此寧可倚外勢周旋，也不肯就範；唐則必須把西域交通納入可控制的秩序，因為安西都護府的佈局、良馬的來源、佛經與使節的往返都依賴這條線。於是衝突從使者與商旅的摩擦，變成兩個政權在絲路口上的一次正面較量。
causeEn: The spark was Qu Wentai's obstruction of the western tributary route. In the Zhenguan years the Tang envoys and merchants went west from Dunhuang through Gaochang, Yanqi and Kucha to the states of the western regions, and Gaochang sat astride the throat of the corridor north and south of the Tian Shan. Qu Wentai had allied with the Western Turks and would not submit to Tang restraint, and envoys who went to him were kept waiting and treated with contempt; to a Tang court that styled itself the Son of Heaven's khan, that was a challenge to the order of the court audience. The fact that Xuanzang on his quest for the scriptures had been received lavishly by Qu Wentai shows as well that the survival of this city-state hung on its position on the Silk Road and on the attitude of the Tang court. At a deeper level Gaochang was a city-state built by Han Chinese settlers, and the strength of the Qu house rested on irrigated farming and on its node position in the caravan trade; the family feared that submitting would cost it its statehood, and so preferred to manoeuvre under foreign protection rather than comply. The Tang, for its part, had to bring the traffic of the western regions into an order it could control, because the deployment of the Protectorate, the supply of fine horses, and the coming and going of scriptures and envoys all depended on that line. The clash therefore began as friction between envoys and merchants and became a set-piece confrontation between two states at a crossroads of the Silk Road.
impact: 高昌國的滅亡改變了天山南北的權力格局。唐以高昌故地置西州，治交河，領交河、蒲昌、柳中、天泉等縣，並在交河置安西都護府；原高昌王麴文泰被追贈太尉、葬於長安北原，麴智盛授官封爵留京，漢人屯戍後裔的二十二座城與八千餘戶被編入唐的版籍。絲路受阻的風險解除，波斯、大食的使節此後經西州入朝，僧侶與貨物的往來在官方護送下進行。戰略上的連鎖同樣重要：貞觀十四年同時解決了高昌與吐蕃圍松州兩件事，唐在西線取得主動，隨後平龜茲、平弓月、擊定漠北，直到開元年間在天山南北建立完整的軍鎮與屯田體系。代價同樣真實：遠征數千里使國庫與民力拉長，麴氏王室的東遷與漢人城邦的消失，使吐魯番盆地原有的灌溉聚落逐漸荒廢，交河故城在九世紀之後淪為廢墟；侯君集因貪污案降職，數年後又牽入太子承乾之案被斬，唐的西域武功與朝廷內部的猜忌由此同時加深。
impactEn: The fall of Gaochang reshaped the balance of power north and south of the Tian Shan. The Tang made the old Gaochang land into Xizhou, seated at Jiuhe and holding the counties of Jiuhe, Puchang, Liuzhong and Tianquan, and set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions at Jiuhe; the former king Qu Wentai was posthumously honoured as Grand Commandant and buried on the northern plain of Chang'an, Qu Zhisheng was granted office and rank and kept at the capital, and the twenty-two towns and eight thousand-odd households of the Han garrison descendants were entered in the Tang registers. The risk of a cut Silk Road was lifted, and envoys from Persia and from the Arab lands thereafter entered the court through Xizhou, with monks and goods travelling under official escort. The chain of strategic consequences mattered as much: in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan the Tang disposed at once of Gaochang and of the Tibetan siege of Songzhou, gained the initiative on the western front, and went on to reduce Kucha, to reduce the Xueyantuo state of Jami, and to settle the steppe north of the desert, until the Kaiyuan era saw a complete system of garrisons and farms established north and south of the Tian Shan. The cost was equally real: an expedition of several thousand li stretched the treasury and the strength of the people; the eastward removal of the Qu house and the end of the Han city-state left the irrigated settlements of the Turpan basin to fall into ruin, and Jiuhe itself was a ruin after the ninth century; and Hou Junji, demoted over the plunder case, was caught up years later in the affair of the crown prince Li Chengqian and executed, so that the Tang western victories and the mutual suspicion inside the court deepened together.
result: 八月進圍之後，唐軍攻破交河城，麴智盛出降，高昌國亡，唐得其城二十二座、戶八千四十六、口一萬七千七百。太宗隨即以高昌故地置西州，設官屬民，置安西都護府治交河，詔葬麴文泰於長安北原而減省其喪儀，麴智盛授官封爵留京師；西州其後設屯田，供安西都護府軍糧，漢人原有的城渠與屯田被唐的郡縣體系接管。戰役的收尾對唐廷並非全然光彩：侯君集入城後不敢禁制將士競盜，又有私取官物，班師遭人舉發而下獄，褚遂良上封事論其貪，太宗貶其官，他與李靖的功業相較而不得拜相，怨望於是種下禍根。就軍事而言，此役的意義在於一次成功的遠征拿下天山孔道的樞紐：唐第一次把安西都護府設在實際控制的土地上，爾後的龜茲、弓月、吐蕃諸役都以交河為後方與跳板，直到北庭都護府立，絲路北道與南道才真正連成一體，高昌的城渠則成為唐王朝在天山南麓經營的起點。
resultEn: After the investment of the eighth month the Tang army breached the city of Jiuhe, Qu Zhisheng came out and surrendered, the state of Gaochang ceased to exist, and the Tang took its twenty-two towns, eight thousand and forty-six households and seventeen thousand seven hundred persons. The emperor at once made the old Gaochang land into Xizhou, appointed officials and registered the people, and established the Protectorate of the Western Regions at Jiuhe; he issued an edict for the burial of Qu Wentai on the northern plain of Chang'an while cutting back the extravagant rites of that burial, and Qu Zhisheng was granted office and rank and kept at the capital. Xizhou later received farms of its own to provision the Protectorate's army, and the old channels and fields of the Han settlers were taken over by the Tang commandery-and-county system. The closing of the campaign was not entirely creditable: once inside the city Hou Junji had not dared to stop his soldiers from plunder, and there was the taking of property besides; on the march back he was impeached and imprisoned, Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial charging him with greed, the emperor demoted him, and measured against a man of Li Jing's achievements he was passed over for the highest ministry, which was the beginning of his misfortune. In military terms the meaning of the war lies in a successful long-range seizure of the hinge of the corridor through the Tian Shan: for the first time the Tang set the Protectorate of the Western Regions on ground it actually held, and the later campaigns against Kucha, against Jami and against Tibet all used Jiuhe as their base and springboard, until the establishment of the Protectorate of the Northern Court joined the northern and southern roads of the Silk Road into one, and the towns and channels of Gaochang became the starting point of Tang rule on the southern foot of the mountains.
